subproblem.title: Upper semicontinuity of the non-β-flat sets under support and domain convergence (supplied proof, step 12; A.3(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, β > 0, S, D ⊆ ℝ^P and S_k, D_k ⊆ ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ). Notation for this statement: for S, D ⊆ ℝ^P and β ∈ ℝ let R(S, D) be the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D, a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with dim Q = n, and s < βρ such that |(y − w) − p_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for every y ∈ S ∩ B_ρ(w) (p_Q = Q.starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto Q); and let N(S, D) := ((S ∩ D) ∖ R(S, D)) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ D). (N(spt μ, D μ) is the set sing'(μ) of the parent proof; in the Lean statement R and N are written out.) Assume: closedBall 0 1 ⊆ D; B_1(0) ⊆ D_k for every k; every compact K ⊆ D satisfies K ⊆ D_k for all sufficiently large k; and whenever sub : ℕ → ℕ is strictly increasing, z_k ∈ S_{sub(k)} for all k, z_k → x and x ∈ D, then x ∈ S. Then for every ε > 0 there is k₀ such that for all k ≥ k₀, B_1(0) ∩ N(S_k, D_k) ⊆ {x : there is z ∈ N(S, D) with |x − z| < ε}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 12 of that proof (A.3(3)), i.e. Simon's claim (lines 539–541) that if y ∈ R_β(S), y_j ∈ spt S_j and y_j → y then y_j ∈ R_β(S_j) for all large j. The support convergence (parent step 8) and the domain convergence (M6) enter here as hypotheses.
Notation in the proof: q_Q(v) := v − p_Q(v). q_Q is linear because p_Q is. |q_Q(v)| ≤ |v|: q_Q(v) ∈ Q^⊥ and p_Q(v) ∈ Q, so |v|² = |p_Q v|² + |q_Q v|² by Pythagoras. In Mathlib, v − Q.starProjection v = Qᗮ.starProjection v (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val), and ‖Qᗮ.starProjection v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le). q_Q is also continuous, being a continuous linear map.
1. (Contradiction hypothesis.) Suppose the conclusion fails for some ε > 0. Then for every k₀ there are k ≥ k₀ and w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ N(S_k, D_k) with |w − z| ≥ ε for all z ∈ N(S, D). Hence (Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop, after choosing w for each such k) there are a strictly increasing κ : ℕ → ℕ and points w_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ N(S_{κ(j)}, D_{κ(j)}) with |w_j − z| ≥ ε for every z ∈ N(S, D) and every j.
2. (Each w_j is a non-flat support point.) w_j ∈ B_1(0) ⊆ D_{κ(j)}, so w_j ∉ ℝ^P ∖ D_{κ(j)}. Since w_j ∈ N(S_{κ(j)}, D_{κ(j)}), w_j ∈ S_{κ(j)} and w_j ∉ R(S_{κ(j)}, D_{κ(j)}).
3. (A limit point.) The w_j lie in the compact set closedBall 0 1. By IsCompact.tendsto_subseq there are a strictly increasing φ and w ∈ closedBall 0 1 with w_{φ(i)} → w. Put σ := κ ∘ φ, which is strictly increasing, and v_i := w_{φ(i)}. Then v_i → w, v_i ∈ S_{σ(i)}, v_i ∉ R(S_{σ(i)}, D_{σ(i)}), and |v_i − z| ≥ ε for z ∈ N(S, D).
4. (w is a β-flat point of S.) w ∈ closedBall 0 1 ⊆ D. The support hypothesis (sub = σ, z_i = v_i, x = w) gives w ∈ S. If w ∈ N(S, D), then |v_i − w| ≥ ε for all i, contradicting v_i → w; so w ∉ N(S, D). As w ∈ S ∩ D and w ∉ (S ∩ D) ∖ R(S, D), we get w ∈ R(S, D). Take ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D, Q with dim Q = n, and s < βρ with |q_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for all y ∈ S ∩ B_ρ(w).
5. (Parameters.) ρ' := (ρ + max(s/β, 0))/2. Since s/β < ρ and 0 < ρ, max(s/β, 0) < ρ, so 0 < ρ' < ρ and ρ' > s/β, i.e. s < βρ' (β > 0). τ := (s + βρ')/2, so s < τ < βρ'. η := (ρ − ρ')/4 > 0, so ρ' + η < ρ. Any choices with 0 < ρ' < ρ, s < βρ', s < τ < βρ' and ρ' + η < ρ work, e.g. obtained with exists_between.
6. (Domains for large i.) K := closedBall w (ρ' + η) is compact and K ⊆ B_ρ(w) ⊆ D. By hypothesis K ⊆ D_k for all large k, and since σ(i) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), K ⊆ D_{σ(i)} for all large i. Also |v_i − w| < η for all large i. For such i, B_{ρ'}(v_i) ⊆ K ⊆ D_{σ(i)}, since |x − w| ≤ |x − v_i| + |v_i − w| < ρ' + η.
7. (Uniform flatness for large i.) Claim: for all large i, |q_Q(y − v_i)| ≤ τ for every y ∈ S_{σ(i)} ∩ B_{ρ'}(v_i). Otherwise, for infinitely many i there is such a y with |q_Q(y − v_i)| > τ. Extract a strictly increasing ψ and points y_l ∈ S_{σ(ψ(l))} ∩ B_{ρ'}(v_{ψ(l)}) with |q_Q(y_l − v_{ψ(l)})| > τ. Since |v_i| < 1, |y_l| < 1 + ρ', so the y_l lie in the compact closedBall 0 (1 + ρ'), and a further strictly increasing χ gives y_{χ(m)} → y'. Put σ' := σ ∘ ψ ∘ χ, which is strictly increasing, and u_m := v_{ψ(χ(m))}, so u_m → w. Then |y' − w| = lim_m |y_{χ(m)} − u_m| ≤ ρ' < ρ, so y' ∈ B_ρ(w) ⊆ D. The support hypothesis (sub = σ', z_m = y_{χ(m)} ∈ S_{σ'(m)}, x = y') gives y' ∈ S. By continuity of q_Q and of the norm, |q_Q(y' − w)| = lim_m |q_Q(y_{χ(m)} − u_m)| ≥ τ > s. This contradicts y' ∈ S ∩ B_ρ(w) and the choice of (ρ, Q, s) in step 4.
8. (Contradiction.) Choose i large enough for steps 6 and 7. Then (ρ', Q, τ) witnesses v_i ∈ R(S_{σ(i)}, D_{σ(i)}): ρ' > 0, B_{ρ'}(v_i) ⊆ D_{σ(i)}, dim Q = n, τ < βρ', and |q_Q(y − v_i)| ≤ τ for y ∈ S_{σ(i)} ∩ B_{ρ'}(v_i). This contradicts step 3 (v_i ∉ R(S_{σ(i)}, D_{σ(i)})). Hence the conclusion holds for every ε > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Assuming failure, extract non-flat w_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ S_{κ(j)}, uniformly ε-far from N(S, D), converging to w ∈ closedBall 0 1 ⊆ D.
Support convergence gives w ∈ S; ε-separation gives w ∉ N(S, D), so w is β-flat with witness (ρ, Q, s).
Shrink to (ρ', Q, τ) with s < τ < βρ'; domain convergence gives B_{ρ'}(v_i) ⊆ D_{σ(i)}, and a compactness/support-convergence argument gives |q_Q(y − v_i)| ≤ τ on S_{σ(i)} ∩ B_{ρ'}(v_i) for large i.
Hence v_i is β-flat for large i, which is a contradiction.

audit.reason: The proof tracks strictly increasing subsequences and their compositions correctly. The closed unit ball lies in D, compact exhaustion supplies the smaller domain balls, and support convergence plus the strict flatness margin excludes escaping support points. This proves the stated eventual inclusion without additional openness or closedness assumptions.
